findings.evidence: Ordinal #20 (8 characters; neither a generic cloud or CI account nor on the release scan's allowlist): 6 matches, one in the `header.json` member of each of the 6 `.eval` logs (member objects 9b6feb8ee59d, 5ac78e51ddfc, 2040b443f665, 754609adf039, 655ac59e381f, 8e86d3ce28fc), under JSON key `location`, the path continuing into a dot-directory (a dataset cache); each `.eval` container holds the same header compressed (of the 85 archive-member findings inside the 6 containers, at most 6 are header copies; the rest are sample members with ordinals #1-#19). It is the same account as PC-ast-survey-agentdojo-13: the survey author's workstation account (the verifier's comparison, names held in memory only). The bare name occurs 0 times in aer/, sem/, prov/, validation/, the index, the register, corpus.json and the raw origin and member rows: the Inspect mapper never copies `eval.dataset` (D-235). Raw only, so CC-11 (S2), not CC-12(a) S0. kexin's `dataset-location-home` pattern matches all 6 headers; no statement covers them (`agentharm-raw-withheld-account-paths` names fragfuse and kexin only). The pre-check missed it (L1-10 screened 0 non-JSON files; the JSON screen did not open the `.eval` header).
findings.recommendation: User decision (sent to the orchestrator 2026-10-24; one decision can cover both survey parts, as D-771 did for PC-13): (a) a D-604 object-scope withhold in survey-agentharm (@1 → @2), anchored on the header key `location` as kexin's `dataset-location-home`, withholding the 6 headers and their containers, then a re-import (1,056 executions); or (b) `pinned-account` plus a datasheet disclosure (D-604 item 7). Recommended: (a). Done: the user chose (a), D-811 (survey-agentharm@2), re-imported as `ast-survey-agentharm-rg2`; its post-check finds residue 0 (see that dossier).
